final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no genuinely new admissible evidence. The response is a reframing of the same evidence toward a narrower position: not clean certification, but certification only if the unresolved limitation is explicitly disclosed. That distinction is analytically useful, but it does not resolve the core compliance predicate. Under the policy text, certification without material caveats requires either no remaining material weakness or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The available record still indicates a remaining named-use-case gap and an incomplete mitigation record, and there is still no admissible evidence that the required disclosure was actually included in the certification artifact or that approved risk acceptance exists. Because the Actor's narrowed position remains conditional on a disclosure that is not evidenced in the record available to this role, the claim remains suspicious rather than moving to compliant_with_caveats. This is not a move toward noncompliance either, because the Actor expressly conceded the limits of the record and did not defend a clean caveat-free certification.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence was provided; the Actor only narrowed the interpretation of the same summarized record.
There is still no admissible certification artifact or decision memo showing the unresolved laboratory-results-routing limitation was actually disclosed at launch.
There is still no admissible approved risk-acceptance record for the named use case.
The mitigation record remains incomplete on the Actor's own account because owner and threshold are still TBD, which does not satisfy the policy condition for avoiding current disclosure.

Aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support launch readiness generally, but they do not by themselves establish compliance with the specific certification-without-caveats policy predicate.
